 Order

Petitioners who are arraigned as accused Nos.5 to 7 have filed this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C seeking anticipatory bail in crime No.99/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 304B, 498A, 504, 506, 149 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (for short, 'IPC'), and under Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short, 'D.P.Act'), contending that they have been falsely implicated in this case.
There are no sufficient material to NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657 substantiate the allegations against them.
The complaint averments are flimsy and are articulated just to meet the ingredients of offences punishable under Sections 304B and 498A of IPC.
Accused Nos.1 to 4 are already granted bail in Crl.P.Nos.103931/2022 and 103933/2022.
The petitioners are not the members of the family of accused Nos.1 to 4 and they are not concerned with the deceased.
There are no specific allegations against them.
If bail is granted they are ready to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and prays to allow the petition.

2. Learned High Court Government Pleader has filed objections stating that after conducting detailed investigation charge sheet is filed against accused Nos.1 to 7 including the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304, 504, 506, 149 IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of D.P. Act.

It is case of the prosecution that about one and half year prior to the date of incident, the deceased-Anita and accused No.1 fell in love with each NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657 other and had eloped, they got married against the wishes of their family members.
After the marriage, deceased was living with all the accused persons.

However, after about six months, accused persons started harassing and ill- treating her stating that she has eloped with accused No.1 or else they would have got dowry in sum of Rs.50,000/-, gold ornaments and other utensils.
They were asking her to die, so that they can perform the second marriage of accused No.1.
They were assaulting and abusing her.

sentences.text: On 12.06.2022 at about 11.00 p.m. Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 picked up quarrel with deceased-Anita and assaulted her.
They asked her to die.
The mother of deceased and neighbours intervening and pacified the galata.

Unable to bear the torture and harassment, in between 11.00 p.m. to 11.30 p.m.
on 12.06.2022, deceased-Anita committed suicide by jumping into pond.
3. There are specific allegations against the petitioners.
After conducting the detailed investigation NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657 charge sheet is filed against all the accused persons including petitioners.
Since from the date of incident petitioners were absconding.
Considering conduct of the petitioners they are not entitled for anticipatory bail and prays to reject the appeal.

4. Heard the arguments and perused the records.
5.
Present petition is filed by the Accused Nos.5 to 7 who are the mother, father and brother of accused No.3.
It is relevant to note that deceased-Anita is no other than the niece of the accused No.2-Mallappa.
She fell in love with accused No.1 and both of them eloped and got married against the wishes of their family members.
From the complaint averments, it is evident that because of this reason, complainant and her family members were not in contact with deceased-Anita.
After the marriage, deceased was living with accused persons.
6. After about five to six months, deceased contacted her sister-Sunita alias Nirmala over phone and NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657 informed her about the ill-treatment.

In this regard, the complainant along with the elders of the village namely 1)Santosh Koppad, 2) Ramesh Koppad, 3) Kannappa Koppad, 4)Parameshappa Koppad, went to the house of accused persons, held panchayat and requested the Accused Nos.1 to 3 not to harass her daughter.
They persisted that if they had married accused No.1 elsewhere, they would got dowry of Rs.50,000/- and gold and other house hold articles.

However, they returned after advising the accused Nos.1 to 3.
7.
On 12.06.2022, in the evening, while the complainant was returning from work, she heard the Commotion in the house of accused persons.

she went there and found all the accused persons including petitioners quarreling with deceased-Anita and abusing her once again saying that they could have got dowry and if she dies, they are going to perform the second marriage of accused No.1 and if she failed to commit suicide, they are NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657 going to kill her.
The complainant intervening and tried to pacified them.
8. During night, complainant came to know that deceased-Anita was not to be found in the house.
They went in search of her and on the next day at about 11.30 a.m., they found her body floating in the pond.

In respect of the said incident, the complaint is filed on 13.06.2022 and case is registered against accused Nos.1 to 7 for the offences punishable under Sections 304B, 498A, 504, 506, 149 of IPC, and under Section 3 and 4 of D.P. Act.
After conducting the detailed investigation charge sheet is filed against all the accused persons including petitioners.
During crime stage, accused Nos.1 to 4 were arrested and were remanded to the judicial custody.
Later on they have secured bail in Crl.P.Nos.103931/2022 and 103933/2022.

sentences.text: Though the petitioners claimed that they are not related to the accused persons, but the charge sheet revealed that petitioners are no other than the father, NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657 mother and brother of accused No.3 and they are the resident of same village.
There are specific allegations against the petitioners.

However, having regard to the fact that already investigation is completed,
the custodial presence of the petitioners are not required.
The apprehension of the prosecution that they may threaten or tamper with the prosecution witnesses may be over come by imposing stringent conditions.
For the above reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioners are entitled for anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

In the event of their arrest Petitioners/accused Nos.5 to 7 shall be released on bail, in Crime No.99/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 304B, 498A, 504, 506, 149 of IPC, and under Section 3 and 4 of D.P. Act,
subject to following:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657 CONDITIONS a) The petitioners/accused No.5 to 7 shall execute personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties each for the like-sum.
b) The petitioners/accused No.5 to 7 shall appear before the investigating officer within a period of 15 days and execute the bail bond and offer surety.
c) The petitioners/accused No.5 to 7 shall furnish their residential address proof and shall inform the investigating officer/Court if there is any change in the address.
d) The petitioners/accused No.5 to 7 shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) The petitioners/accused No.5 to 7 shall not indulge in any criminal activities.
- 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC-D:8657  f) The petitioners/accused No.5 to 7 shall  be regular in attending the Court  proceedings.
